title: Sunrise Health - Redwood onboarding kickoff
summary: Kickoff for Sunrise Health onboarding to Redwood. Covered introductions, success criteria, infra/network constraints (VPC, firewall, KMS), hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs, pilot scope, and next steps for SSO, security docs, and SOW.
topics: Deployment options: hosted vs dedicated vs private
next_steps: Redwood to send onboarding guide & SOW
Schedule infra deep-dive with Samir and Ethan (network/VPC)
Customer to provide list of sample workloads & qps targets
Set up trial keys and demo project by 2026-05-18
action_items: Maya Patel - Send onboarding guide + SOW - 2026-05-18
Ethan Li - Schedule infra deep-dive and prepare network diagram notes - 2026-05-20
Samir Khan - Share VPC peering/VPN details and firewall rules - 2026-05-19
Priya Rao - Create kickoff timeline and onboarding playbook for Success team - 2026-05-21
header:
Date: 2026-05-14
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Alex (Sunrise CTO), Dana (Sunrise Head Eng), Samir (Sunrise Cloud Ops), Lina (Sunrise Product)
transcript: 00:00 - Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're really excited to kick this off with Sunrise Health. quick round of intros?
00:12 - Alex (Sunrise - CTO): Hi all, Alex here, CTO. we'll be owning the integration side, Dana will lead eng, Samir is our cloud ops, Lina on product. thanks Maya.

00:28 - Maya (Redwood AE): awesome, quick intro from our side: I'm Maya, I'll be your AE and primary contact; Ethan is our SE who will handle infra and performance stuff, and Priya is your CSM for onboarding and post-launch success.
00:45 - Ethan (Redwood - SE): hey team, yea excited. i'll dig into the network/VPC parts and the pilot test plan. quick note, apologies in advance for any audio glitches, I'm on a train, ha.

01:05 - Dana (Sunrise - Head Eng): no worries. curiosity up front: our main constraints are HIPAA-ish data residency and strict egress controls. we want to understand private deployment options and if hosted can meet our needs.

01:35 - Priya (Redwood CSM): totally hear you, we'll walk through options. typical path is start with a small pilot on Redwood Hosted with a dedicated project/keys, then move to Dedicated or Private depending on residency and SLA needs.
02:02 - Alex: timeline question — we want pilot live in ~3 weeks, production in ~8-10 weeks. is that realistic?

02:15 - Maya: yes, that's reasonable. pilot in three weeks is doable if we get infra access and sample data/queries. full prod timing depends on whether you go Private (VPC/on-prem) which adds lead time for network and KMS setup.
02:40 - Samir (Sunrise Cloud Ops): on VPC: we have strict firewall rules, no public outbound on our compute subnets; we can do VPC peering or private link. any docs for required endpoints?

02:58 - Ethan: we have a VPC peering playbook and a minimal firewall rule list; we'll send that after this call. also note, if you do Dedicated, peering is usually easiest; for Hosted we can support Private Networking via our Private deployment options — there are tradeoffs on latency and cost.

03:20 - Lina (Product): success criteria from our side: <1s latency for short prompts under 64 tokens, average cost per 1k tokens under $X (they didn't want to commit to a value on the call), and no PHI leaving controlled systems — so encryption and auditability are key.

03:50 - Maya: got it. we'll capture that as pilot SLAs: latency target, cost goals, and security requirements. on PHI, we can support customer-managed KMS and audit logs — Ethan will walk through the KMS flow.

04:10 - Ethan: right — from a KMS perspective we support bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via KMS/HSM integrations. there's an extra provisioning step for private deployments. small note: our docs sometimes say KV cache as 'key-value cache' but transcripts and docs sometimes show 'K V cache' so ignore that noise in the doc, ha.
04:40 - Dana: that's helpful. do you have SOC2 or ISO reports? our procurement requires SOC2 Type II and an inventory of logging/audit capabilities.
04:55 - Priya: yes, Redwood has SOC2 Type II. we'll share the latest report and the security whitepaper. we'll also send a checklist for your security review and the relevant audit log examples.
05:15 - Alex: great. procurement will want to see where data is stored by default — are hosted deployments multi-region? can we pin region?

05:30 - Ethan: hosted allows region pinning in supported regions; Dedicated and Private give you full control over region and hosting. for pilot we suggest region pinning to reduce latency and meet residency needs.
06:00 - Samir: about traffic patterns — we expect spikes up to 200 qps for search-like workloads and lower for conversational features. do you have autoscale and burst capacity for that?

06:20 - Ethan: yes, Dedicated supports autoscaling and burst capacity; hosted has configurable throttles and predictable charing tiers. we'll map your qps to instance sizes and give recommendations—typically batching and prefix caching reduce token cost and effective throughput.
06:50 - Dana: can Redwood's runtime do quantized models? we're evaluating cost tradeoffs vs accuracy.

07:05 - Ethan: yes, we support quantization-friendly execution paths and selections based on model profiles. we'll propose model/quantization configurations during the pilot. note that quantization can impact latency/quality tradeoffs.
07:35 - Maya: ok practical next step: we'll send onboarding guide + SOW and trial keys. Ethan and Samir will schedule an infra deep-dive to cover VPC peering, firewall rules, and KMS.
07:55 - Alex: would you also run a small benchmark using one of our sample prompts so we can see latency/cost numbers?
08:10 - Ethan: yes, please share 5-10 canonical prompts and representative traffic pattern. we'll run a benchmark on a matching model variant and send results in the benchmark spreadsheet.
08:30 - Lina: timeline: we'll aim to send prompts and sample payload by EOD Monday (2026-05-17).

08:40 - Priya: perfect — after we receive that we'll provision trial keys and the test project, then schedule the benchmark run. we'll also surface recommended model configs and initial cost estimates.
09:05 - Dana: on compliance, we also need SSO (SAML) and RBAC in the Console. do you support SCIM/SSO?

09:20 - Maya: yes, SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning are supported for enterprise accounts. we will include the SSO integration doc in the packet we send. for RBAC we have role templates and you can map to your IdP groups.
09:45 - Samir: any enterprise-level logging retention? we need audit logs to be retained for at least 90 days and exportable to our SIEM.

09:58 - Ethan: audit logs are configurable and we support exporting to S3 or a secure syslog endpoint; retention windows can be increased on Dedicated/Private. we'll include examples of the audit log schema.
10:20 - Alex: cost question: what's the billing model for Dedicated vs Hosted for trial stage?

10:35 - Maya: for pilot we typically offer usage-based billed Hosted (per token) with trial credits. Dedicated has a reserved capacity contract; for pilot we can do a short reserved window or a burst-enabled eval — we'll include options in the SOW.
10:55 - Dana: procurement may ask for an NDA and MSA; is there a standard MSA you use?
11:10 - Priya: yes we have a standard MSA and procurement-ready templates; we'll share the MSA, NDA, and SOC2. if you have redlines, we can loop legal in next week.

11:30 - Maya: ok recapping: Redwood to send onboarding guide, SOW options, SOC2 and security docs, SSO doc, audit log examples; Sunrise to send sample prompts, traffic profile, and VPC/firewall contact details. we'll schedule infra deep-dive for next week.
11:55 - Alex: that matches our notes. ETA for docs from Redwood?
12:05 - Maya: we'll send the packet by Monday 2026-05-18. Ethan will reach out to Samir to schedule the infra session — target 2026-05-20.
12:25 - Samir: sounds good. i also want a simple checklist of ports/endpoints so I can triage with our network team quickly.

12:40 - Ethan: I'll include a one-page firewall checklist in the packet; it lists endpoints, ports, and recommended NAT/peering settings. small caveat: some internal doc names may have typos (e.g., 'KV cache' indexing), so use the network checklist as canonical.
13:05 - Lina: one more ask — can Redwood redact PII/PHI at rest or is that something we need to handle?

13:20 - Priya: we don't perform automatic ingestion redaction by default; we recommend a pre-processing step on your side for guaranteed redaction, but we do support DLP integrations and tokenization patterns; we can document options.
13:45 - Alex: good to know. okay anyone else? if not let's wrap and confirm the next steps.
14:00 - Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the packet and SOW. action items recorded. Priya will own the onboarding timeline. speak soon!
14:15 - Dana: thanks all, bye.
14:20 - (Call ends)
Note: Transcript contains occasional transcription artifacts and minor misattributions typical of automated meeting notes.
